text:
alex.moore: quick check on embeddings endpoint behaviour — i started a small smoke test and hit a few questions.

maria.kim: go ahead, what did you see?

alex.moore: sending mixed inputs (empty string, null, very long text) in one batch. API accepted an array with a null item but returned vectors shifted by one in one of my runs. not sure if client bug or server coercion.

samir: can you paste the exact request body you used?

alex.moore: sure — i used the python client but here is the raw payload i sent to /v1/embeddings:

```json
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-1",
  "input": ["hello world", "", null, "longtext..."],
  "truncate": "end",
  "max_tokens": 8192
}
```

alex.moore: response looked like this (redacted):

```json
{
  "data": [
    {"object":"embedding","embedding":[0.001, -0.12, ...]},
    {"object":"embedding","embedding":[0.0, 0.0, ...]},
    {"object":"embedding","embedding":null},
    {"object":"embedding","embedding":[0.12, 0.03, ...]}
  ],
  "model": "redwood-embed-1",
  "usage": {"input_tokens": 12345}
}
```

alex.moore: the weird bit was the second vector looked like a zero-vector placeholder rather than a real embed for the empty string, and the null stayed null. i expected either all items to be coerced to strings before encoding ("null" -> "null") or the server to return an explicit error for null items.

maria.kim: current contract (per the API docs draft) says: inputs are coercible to strings, empty strings are allowed and produce deterministic vectors, nulls are rejected with 400. so this result sounds like partial coercion + placeholder behavior — not intended.

jin-l: tagging @ops-bot for logs. ops-bot: did the request ID alex.shared show any upstream transformation?

ops-bot: automated: request 7f3a1c logged. incoming payload contained a JSON null at index 2. No automatic coercion executed. Server routed to embed-worker-7. Worker returned 207 multi-status due to partial processing (empty item fallback applied). Full trace attached in infra (link).

samir: ok, high level proposals: (1) strict: reject any null in input with 400, docs updated; (2) permissive: coerce null to empty string and return deterministic vector; (3) hybrid: allow null but return explicit object: {"object":"embedding","error":"null input"} to keep positions stable. Thoughts?

maria.kim: leaning to hybrid. it preserves indexing and avoids silent zero-vectors. also simpler for clients to detect per-item errors. we should document that behavior and add SDK helpers.

alex.moore: hybrid sounds good. also a separate thing: truncation semantics. i sent a very long item and set truncate: end. i expected last tokens kept; response seemed to indicate tokenizer truncation at 2048 tokens despite max_tokens 8192. is there an internal per-item cap?

samir: yes — runtime currently enforces per-item sequence cap based on model profile (redwood-embed-1 has 2048 seq cap) to protect memory. max_tokens is a global/route limit we added but per-item cap overrides it. we should make that explicit in the API ("per_input_token_limit").

maria.kim: action item: add per_input_token_limit to /v1/embeddings response meta and to docs. PR to SDKs to expose this as EmbeddingResponse.token_limits. alex, can you file the docs + SDK issue?

alex.moore: will do. i'll open two PRs: docs + python client change to surface per-item errors and token limits.

jin-l: batch limits: what's current max batch size? i think we have 1024 items for dedicated, 128 for hosted tier-1?

samir: hosted default is 256 items per request, but we have autosplit in the gateway for larger batches up to 1024 if customer is on higher quota. but that autosplit does per-slice truncation independently which can change ordering if not careful. gateway should preserve ordering by concatenating results in original order — if we autosplit into slices we must ensure we map results back correctly.

alex.moore: the ordering bug i saw might be from a race in the gateway when a slice returned a 207 with per-item errors. mapping got misaligned. i'll attach logs to the issue.

maria.kim: let's be explicit in contract: response.data array must be same length & order as input array. each element is either {"object":"embedding", "embedding": [floats]} or {"object":"error", "error": "reason"}. no nulls and no implicit zero placeholders.

samir: agreed. also add a top-level "per_input_token_limit" and "batch_slice_count" (if autosplit occurred) fields to help clients.

alex.moore: PR checklist i'll open: 1) docs: add explicit rules for null/empty; 2) server: return error objects for nulls; 3) gateway: fix ordering when merging slices; 4) SDK: expose per-item errors and token limits; 5) add unit tests for mixed inputs + large batch.

maria.kim: timeline?

alex.moore: i'll aim to open PRs today for docs + python SDK. samir can take server/gateway change, target end of week for patch. jin-l can validate SLO/regressions on staging.

jin-l: i'll run a full regression on 3k synthetic batches tomorrow morning. will report back in this thread.

ops-bot: automated: created ticket EMB-4327 (embeddings: per-item error objects + ordering guarantees).

maria.kim: thanks — once PRs are up ping me for a quick review.

alex.moore: thanks everyone, i'll post links when PRs exist. :thumbsup:
